text: I honestly think having my phone with me all the time hurts my focus way more than it helps, even though I always tell myself it's fine. Like I can convince myself I need it for the timer or for looking up a word, but really it just sits there waiting to interrupt me. The second I get a notification my whole train of thought is gone and it takes forever to get back into whatever I was doing. Last semester this got really bad when I was trying to write a paper for my history class the night before it was due. I had my phone face up next to my laptop and every few minutes someone in my group chat would text, and I kept telling myself I'd just answer real quick and then keep writing. But then real quick turned into twenty minutes of scrolling and I looked up and it was already past midnight and I had basically written nothing. When I finally put the phone in my desk drawer across the room, something kind of clicked and I actually wrote three pages in like an hour, which honestly shocked me. So to me the constant connection isn't really connection at all, it's just a bunch of little interruptions that pretend to be important, and the only time I do deep work is when the phone is somewhere I can't reach it.
